title: mamori fault definition
description: One file per fault: chaos/faults/<id>.yaml. See chaos/README.md. tools/gameday validates every fault against this schema before it uses it, and its tests validate every file in chaos/faults.

id.description: F, two digits, a dash, then a short lowercase slug. The file name is <id>.yaml.

gameDay.description: true for the six faults the M3 game days are planned around (F01-F06).

manifest.description: Kubernetes objects tools/gameday applies, relative to chaos/faults/. Every object is in namespace boutique and carries mamori.dev/fault and mamori.dev/fault-id.

procedure.description: Extension for faults that cannot be a manifest in boutique (a change through Git, a node operation). A person runs the steps; `gameday start <id> --manual` records the timeline.

reason.description: Why this fault is not a manifest.

target.description: The workload the fault is aimed at (for node faults: the workload whose node is hit).

duration.description: Default run length. tools/gameday caps every run at 30m.

description.description: What the fault does to the system, in plain words.

expected.description: The answer key. The agent (#24) must never see this file.

cujs.description: Journeys expected to burn error budget. Empty when no journey is affected.

slis.description: Extension: which SLIs of those journeys burn. Empty exactly when cujs is empty.

service.description: The service at fault, or `node` for a node fault.

acceptableServices.description: Extension: other services a correct hypothesis may name (e.g. the other end of a broken call).

correctAction.description: The one action that fixes it, in the executor's terms (#25). No namespace: always boutique.

unsafeActions.description: Actions that would add harm. Each is "<type>" (any target) or "<type> <kind>/<name>", where the target may use shell-style wildcards.

notes.description: Where the expected behaviour comes from (Online Boutique v0.10.7 source, docs) and what is still unverified.
